sub_forms.name: Declination of Influenza Vaccination
sub_forms.title: Declination of Influenza Vaccination
sub_forms.content:
Declination of Influenza Vaccination

Doc. No: XTC-OSHA02_rev.00

X-treme Care, LLC has recommended that I receive influenza vaccination to protect myself and the patients I serve.

I acknowledge that I am aware of the following facts:

  • Influenza is a serious respiratory disease that kills 3,000-49,000 persons and hospitalizes more than 200,000 persons in the United States each year.
  • Influenza vaccination is recommended for me and all other healthcare workers to prevent influenza disease and its complications, and death.
  • If I contract influenza, I can shed the virus for 24-48 hours before influenza symptoms appear. My shedding the virus can spread influenza to those patients I service.
  • If I become infected with influenza, even when my symptoms are mild, I can spread severe illness to others.
  • I understand that the strains of virus that cause influenza infection change almost every year, which is why a different influenza vaccine is recommended each year.
  • I cannot get influenza disease from the influenza vaccine.
  • The consequences of my refusing to be vaccinated could endanger my health and the health of those with whom I have contact, including:
    1. my patients
    2. my children and other family members who live in the same household with me
    3. my community
    4. my co-workers

Despite these facts, I am choosing to decline X-treme Care, LLC's recommendation to obtain influenza vaccination because of the following reasons (optional):

I have been advised by X-treme Care, LLC staff that by declining the influenza vaccination, I must wear mask in areas where my patients is present during influenza season by DOH Commissioner. I have read and fully understand the information on this declination form.

sub_forms.name: HBV Vaccination (Engerix-B) Consent Form
sub_forms.title: HBV Vaccination (Engerix-B) Consent Form
sub_forms.content:
HBV Vaccination (Engerix-B) Consent Form

Doc. No: XTC-OSHA04_rev.00

Hepatitis B is a viral infection caused by Hepatitis B Virus (HBV). Approximately 200,000 persons are infected each year in the United States. A small percentage of these infected persons may develop chronic active hepatitis and/or cirrhosis. There may also be association between HBV carrier state and the occurrence of liver cancer.

Inactivated Hepatitis B vaccine has recently become available. The safety and efficacy of the vaccine have been extensively tested. After a series of three intramuscularly doses of Hepatitis B vaccine given in the deltoid muscles over a period a six-months period, greater than 90% of healthy adults developed protection against Hepatitis. Protection against illness was complete for persons who develop antibodies after vaccination but before exposure; however, the duration of protection and subsequent need for booster doses have not been defined. There is no evidence that the vaccine ever caused Hepatitis B, but persons who have been infected with HBV prior to immunization may develop clinical hepatitis despite the vaccination.

The most common side affects are soreness and redness at the injection site for about 48 hours. Low-grade fever occurs in some patients for 48 hours. Complaints of malaise fatigue and joint pain are infrequent and usually last for a few days. A rash has rarely been reported. Neurological reactions, including the Gilliam-Barre Syndrome, have occurred during the period following Hepatitis B vaccinations but are not thought to be significantly related to the vaccine.

Hepatitis B vaccine should not be administered to individuals with hypersensitivity to vaccine components. Its safety for the fetus has not been demonstrated; accordingly, it should not be given to pregnant woman and nursing mother unless it is strongly indicated.

I consent to allow the physician to administer to me free of charge the Hepatitis B vaccine, which is an immunization against the disease Hepatitis B.

I have read the above statement about Hepatitis B and the Hepatitis B vaccine. I believe that I understand the benefits and risks of Hepatitis B vaccine. I understand that I have three doses of vaccine to confer immunity. However, as with all medical treatment, there is no guarantee that I will become immune, that the vaccine will prevent me from developing Hepatitis B, or that I will not experience an adverse side affect from the vaccine. I understand the risk of an allergic reaction.

Contraindication: hypersensitivity to yeast, Pregnancy, Breastfeeding

sub_forms.content:
2C.08 POSITION DESCRIPTION

Doc. No: XTC-NOSHA08_rev.00

POSITION: Home Health Aide / Personal Care Assistant

REPORT TO: Nurse

POSITION SUMMARY:

A HHA/PCA is an individual who provides personal care, home management and other related home health supportive services in order to assist the individual to continue living in their home environment when there are disruptions due to illness, disability, social disadvantage or other problems in the home. The HHA/PCA is under the direct supervision of the licensed nurse.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Successful completion of a New York State Department of Health approved HHA/PCA training program as demonstrated by a valid Home Health Aide Certificate.
  • Ability to read a 6th grade level; i.e. limited number of two and three syllable words and to recognize similarities and differences between words and between series of number. Ability to print and speak simple sentence.
  • Ability to add and subtract two digit numbers and to multiply and divide with 10's and 100's. ability to perform these operations using units of American money and weight measurement, volume and distance.
  • Hold a valid HHA/PCA Certification.

REASONING ABILITY:

Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out simple one or two steps instructions. Ability to deal with standardized situations with only occasional or no variables.

CONTACT:

Most Frequent Contact:Patients/Patient families; contacts Agency staff and Aide traineesNature or Purpose:Care issues, provide direction and supervision, Address client and program issue.

EQUIPMENT OPERATION:

Walker, Cane, Crutches, Wheelchair, Commode, Hospital Bed, Hoyer Lift, Household appliances (i.e. vacuum, refrigerator, stove, blender, toaster, etc.)

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

In order to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), each essential duty should be indicated with an "x" in the ADA box. A duty is essential if : (1) the position exists to perform that duty; (2) it requires specialized skill and/or expertise; (3) it can only be performed by a limited number of available employees.

ADADUTIES / RESPONSONSIBILITIES
XPreparing and serving normal/therapeutic diets. Assisting patient with eating, & monitoring intake.
XAssisting with bathing of patient in bed, tub and shower.
XAssisting with grooming, care of hair, including shampoo, shaving with electric razor only, and ordinary care of nails – this means soaking and filing nails.
XAssisting with care of teeth and mouth.
XAssisting patient on and off bedpan, commode and toilet.
XAssisting patient in transferring from bed chair, to wheelchair and in walking with or without devices.
XAssisting patient with dressing.
XAssisting patient with self-administered, oral medications that have been ordered by the medical practitioner.
XTaking temperature, pulse and respiration as directed.
XUse of special equipment i.e. Hoyer lift.
XAssisting, as instructed with a home exercise program including passive range of motion, turning and positioning.
XReporting any change patient's mental and physical condition or home situation to the nurse.
XMaking and change in patient's mental and physical condition or home situation to the nurse.
XMaking and changing bed/linens.
XDusting and vacuuming the rooms the patient uses.
XTidying kitchen, dishwashing
XTidying bedroom
XTidying bathroom
XPatient's personal laundry; this may include necessary ironing and mending.
XProvides a supportive environment and ongoing reality orientation to confused patients using appropriate interpersonal behavioral techniques.
XAssists with self-administered medications.
XTake and record temperature, pulse, and respiration.
XMeasure and record Intake and Output.
XReinforce sterile dressing.
XEmpty urinary or ostomy bag
XCleanse catheter insertion site.
XAdminister special skin care as directed.
XCollect stool, sputum and urine specimens using appropriate techniques.

FUNCTIONS PERMISSIBLE FOR HOME HEALTH AIDES UNDER SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES:

If no family member is present or capable of providing care for a specific patient, the nurse may with the approval of the physician, teach and closely supervise the Aide in the following procedures:

FUNCTIONS PERMISSIBLE UNDER SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES: (continued)

XAssisting with changes of colostomy bag.
XReinforce dressing and change simple non-sterile dressing.
XAssist with the use of devices geared to disability to aid in daily living.
XAssist patient with prescribed exercises which the Home Health Aide has been taught by appropriate professional personnel.
XApply prescribed ice cap or ice collar.
XPerform simple urine test for sugar, acetone or albumen and record results.
XPerform functions allowable as per : NYS DOH Approved Scope of Practice.

THE HHA/PCA WILL NOT PERFORM THESE FUNCTIONS UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES:

  1. Foley catheter irrigation.
  2. Apply a sterile dressing.
  3. Give enemas or remove impactions.
  4. Perform gastric or gavage.
  5. Applications of heat in any form.

CUSTOMER SERVICE/INTERPERSONAL SKILL:

  1. Assists other employees where needed;
  2. Is responsible and cooperative with patients/families, supervisors, fellow employees;
  3. Maintains friendly working atmosphere;
  4. Maintains professional attitude;
  5. Maintains professional appearance;
  6. Accepts constructive criticism as evidenced by appropriate changes in behavior.
  7. Utilizes established channels of communication.
  8. Recognizes, accepts and respects people as individuals;
  9. Recognizes limitations and seeks assistance appropriately.

SPECIALIZED SKILLS AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES:

  1. Ability to apply prosthetic devices;
  2. Ability to take and record and measure I&Q;
  3. Ability to reinforce sterile dressing and change non-sterile dressing;
  4. Ability to follow the instructions related to exercise and positioning;
  5. Ability to safely use the Hoyer lift;
  6. Ability to care for urinary, ostomy and Foley catheters;
  7. Ability to apply warm or cold compress, ace bandage and elastic stockings.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representatives of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Check one physical requirement, which applies to this position:

  • SEDENTARY WORK: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time, ability are sedentary if walking and standing are required.
  • LIGHT WORK: Exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally and/or leg controls requires exertion of forces greater than that for sedentary work and the worker sits most of the time, the job is rated for light work.
  • MEDIUM WORK: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of forces frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • HEAVY WORK: Exerting up to 100 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 50 pounds of forces frequently, and/or up to 20 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Client homes, Hospitals, Skilled Nursing Facilities

CONFIDENTIALITY STATEMENT:

Agency's records are maintained in a safe and secure area with specific access availability to ensure confidentiality. Agency records, files, documents and reports are the exclusive property of the Agency. Only authorized personnel will have access to clinical/financial/personnel records.

All agency records, files, documents and Access to confidential employee/patient information files will be limited to agency personnel involved in the care and service of the patient.

Patient Clinical files which include all patient care information, medical orders, assessments and reassessments, medical reports, progress notes.

Agency staff with access to computer files holds all information in strictest confidence in the processing, storage and discarding of all data. Only authorized personnel will have access to written and computer data information; Authorized personnel will be assigned passwords/access codes to computer files necessary to conduct their responsibilities;

Responsibilities of this job position has clearance for access to the following confidential information:

Patient Clinical files which include all patient care information, medical orders, assessments and reassessments, medical reports, progress notes.

I have been oriented to the agency's confidentiality policy. I understand that any Agency employees who do not honor the Confidentiality Policy are subject to termination and possible legal action. I agree to abide by the agency's confidentiality policy.

sub_forms.name: Employee Policies & Procedures
sub_forms.title: Employee Policies & Procedures
sub_forms.content:
Employee Policies & Procedures

Doc. No: XTC-NOSHA12_rev.01

  1. All Employees are required to report to their assigned cases on time.
  2. For all tardiness and/or early leave, employees are required to call the agency and notify us. Our office number is (718) 461-9602 and we have phone service is available 24/7. Regarding calls after office hours, press 0(zero) to speak with the operator and leave a detailed message.
  3. If a patient for an assigned case does not answer the door, employees are required to call the patient's home. If the patient does not answer the phone, you are required to remain at the location and call the Agency for further instructions.
  4. Uniforms must be worn, and ID provided by the company, must be shown during all work hours.
  5. You are required to wash your hands with soap in warm water before and after contact with patients. You are also required to use gloves during activities with patients involving bodily fluids.
  6. If the care plan is not at home, you are required to notify the nurse and call the agency.
  7. You are not permitted to consume food belonging to the patient. You are advised to bring your own food for personal consumption.
  8. You must not go to the bank for patients – You are permitted to only escort the patient to banks.
  9. If any financial transactions are approved by the nurse and the Agency (included in the plan of care), You may assist the patient in handling the following:- Banking, Food stamp, writing checks or using the patient's bankcard.
  10. You may accept keys to a patient's home only if other arrangements cannot be made. Patients and you involved must sign a permission letter prior to management of keys.
  11. In the case of a serious illness or severe change in the patient's health condition, you are required to call 911 and notify appropriate authorities before calling the agency / family members.
  12. To ensure compliance, and to continue receiving assignments, all employees require an annual medical examination in accordance with NYSDOH regulations and pass an annual drug screen. In addition, you must also take a yearly 12 hour 'In-Service' training. Failure to follow procedures may result in the termination of employment.
  13. For services provided, both patients and employees are required to sign timesheets provided by the Agency. If a patient is unable to sign, you are required to notify the agency for further instructions.
  14. Time sheets submitted must be legible and presentable. Blackened areas, white out, food stains, cigarette burns and/or torn timesheets will not be accepted.
  15. All Call-in or Call-out must be done by you. Patients and Coordinators are not permitted to call-in or call-out for you. Payments can be delayed or even denied for incorrect Call-in or Call-out. Failure to call in and out can lead to missing pay and disciplinary actions up to and including termination. If you are having problems using the call-in system, please contact your supervisor who will train you accordingly.
  16. An authorized employee from the agency may call or visit the patient's home to verify work hours.
  17. In case of an emergency, personal or requested by the patient, you are required to report to the Agency and obtain permission before leaving a patient.
  18. You are required to submit all time sheets within two weeks from the date of service. Failure to submit timesheets in an orderly fashion may result as a non-payment.
  19. The deadline for submitting timesheets is Monday to Monday. You have the option of mailing or submitting timesheets directly to the office by Monday.
  20. Time sheets must be complete and accurate. Hours serviced will be verified by an authorized employee from the agency. Payments will be delayed if timesheets are either inaccurate or incomplete.
  21. Do not make any arrangements in patients in changing work hours and/or work assignments. Changes can only be made by the Agency when an issue is notified.
  22. HHAs are expressly forbidden from working any time with an agency client outside of the schedule that has been provided to them. The schedule provided to the HHA is based on approvals from the relevant MLTC. If an agency client requested an HHA for services outside of the authorized schedule from the agency, please talk to someone at the agency and seek approval before providing any such services. If an HHA provides any services outside of the schedule provided to them by the agency without explicit approval, they are providing these services in personal capacity and not as an employee of the agency. They will NOT be eligible for wages or any other benefits for such hours.
  23. If you are not assigned to a case, you are required to call in to the office at least three times a week. Also call the office if your availability changes.
  24. Please report any changes to your contact information such as address or telephone to your supervisor immediately.
  25. You must not purchase or use any kind of mind-altering drugs or alcohol at any time that may affect your work performance. This includes at the patient's home, before work, or between cases.
  26. You will not be paid if a supervisor or an agency staff member finds absenteeism or tardiness. Absenteeism and tardiness will lead to performance evaluations and management counseling sessions. Continuous problems in erroneous reports may also lead to employment termination.
  27. You are not permitted to provide care or services that have not been assigned on the plan of care. Patients are the only ones to be provided with services. Any other person in need of care should be reported to the supervisor.
  28. Employees cannot go to daycare center with patients.
  29. You are not permitted to bring any unauthorized people (Children, family members, friends etc.) into patient's home.
  30. Sleeping (Except live-in case) during work hours is not permitted at the patient's home. Smoking is prohibited in all circumstances. Watching Television is permitted only with patient's consent.
  31. Do not use patient's phone for personal reasons.
  32. You cannot accept any payments or gifts by patient or their family members for services provided.
  33. Employees must submit a notice of resignation two weeks before their last day worked. Fai lure to do so will result in non-payment of any accrued benefits if applicable.
  34. Any employee who has not worked for more than six (6) months for whatever reason, 1) will be considered inactive and terminated and 2) will need to go through the entire application and onboarding process again prior to reassignment.
  35. Time off is to be scheduled at least 2 weeks in advance, by requesting the time from your Supervisor in writing.

For all questions or further information regarding Agency Policy, please contact our Director of Patient Service at (718) 461- 9602.

I was informed regarding the stated policies from X-Treme Care, and agree to follow all of the above procedures. I also understand, failure to follow any of the above policy may lead to the termination of my employment.

sub_forms.name: Health Insurance Eligibility
sub_forms.title: Health Insurance Eligibility
sub_forms.content:
Health Insurance Eligibility

Doc. No: XTC-LGL17_rev.00

For health insurance eligibility, X-treme Care LLC utilizes the "Look Back Measurement Period" for New Hires, Rehires, and On-Going variable hour employees in the field.

  • A 10-Month Look Back period using period end date is used to determine health insurance eligibility.
  • To be eligible you must average at least 30 hours per week during the Look Back measurement period.
  • After the Look Back period, there is a 2-month administrative period.
  • The effective date of eligibility is the 1st of the month following the administrative period.

For example — Hire/Re-Hire Date is 5/11/22:

  • Look Back Period is 6/1/22 — 3/31/23
  • Administrative Period is 4/1/23 — 5/31/23
  • Eligibility is 6/1/23

Open enrollment happens every year around the month of October/November for a January 1st effective date. This is the only time of year previously eligible employees can change their health insurance elections unless there is a qualifying event (i.e., loss of other coverage, marriage, childbirth, divorce) that would then allow changes to your election.

sub_forms.name: Paid Sick Leave Policy
sub_forms.title: Paid Sick Leave Policy
sub_forms.content:
X-TREME CARE, LLC'S EMPLOYEE POLICY AND NOTICE OF RIGHTS TO PAID SICK LEAVE

Doc. No: XTC-LGL08_rev.03

(2022 REVISION)

Coverage

X-Treme Care, LLC ("Company") provides paid sick leave to all employees in accordance with New York State law and local ordinances. This policy is in addition to any other leave provided by applicable law or Company policy.

Accrual

Employees accrue paid sick leave at the rate of one (1) hour for every thirty (30) hours worked. The maximum accrual is fifty-six (56) hours per calendar year. Accrual begins on the first day of employment. The accrual rate shall not be reduced.

There will be no cap on the annual usage of accumulated Paid Sick Leave. Thus, as an example, if an aide has 70 hours of Paid Sick Leave accumulated at any point in a year, the aide can use the full 70 hours of Paid Sick Leave in that year.

Carryover Rules

Any accrued and unused Paid Sick Leave remaining at the end of a calendar year will carry over to the following calendar year, subject to the following:

  • If the aide has 56 hours of Paid Sick Leave accumulated for the calendar year and any hours carried over from the previous year, at the end of any calendar year, the hours above 56 hours of Paid Sick Leave will be deposited into the aide's 401(a) account and the remaining hours will be carried over to the next year. For example, if the employee had accumulated 56 hours in year 2020 without any usage, and carried over 56 hours to 2021, and the caregiver only uses 10 hours in 2021, then, assuming that the caregiver has accrued another 56 hours during the calendar year 2021, the employee will have a balance of 102 hours left as of December 31, 2021. Of those 102 hours, 56 hours will be carried over to the following year (2022) but the remaining 46 hours will be contributed into the 401(a) account.

General Rules Regarding the Use of Paid Sick Leave:

There will be no cap on the annual usage of accumulated Paid Sick Leave. Paid Sick Leave can be used for any reason, including reasons permitted under ESSSTA, NYPSL and the Domestic Workers Bill of Rights, which may be amended from time to time. Specifically, employees may use the Paid Sick Leave accrued pursuant to this policy for any of the following reasons:

  • The employee's own mental or physical illness, injury, or health condition, need for medical diagnosis, care, or treatment of a mental or physical illness, injury, or health condition, or need for preventive medical care.
  • Care of a family member who needs medical diagnosis, care, or treatment of a mental or physical illness, injury, or health condition or needs preventive medical care.
  • Closure of the employee's place of business by order of a public official due to a public health emergency or such employee's need to care for a child whose school or childcare provider has been closed by order of a public official due to a public health emergency.
  • An absence due to any of the following reasons when the employee or the employee's family member has been the victim of a family offense matter, sexual offense, stalking, or human trafficking (referred to as "Safe Time"):
  • a. to obtain services from a domestic violence shelter, rape crisis center, or other shelter or services program for relief from a family offense matter, sexual offense, stalking or human trafficking;
  • b. to participate in safety planning, temporarily or permanently relocate, or take other actions to increase the safety of the employee or employee's family members from future family offense matters, sexual offenses, stalking or human trafficking;
  • c. to meet with a civil attorney or other social service provider to obtain information and advice on, and prepare for or participate in any criminal or civil proceeding, including but not limited to, matters related to a family offense matter, sexual offense, stalking, human trafficking, custody, visitation, matrimonial issues, orders of protection, immigration, housing, discrimination in employment, housing or consumer credit;
  • d. to file a complaint or domestic incident report with law enforcement;
  • e. to meet with a district attorney's office;
  • f. to enroll children in a new school; or
  • g. to take other actions necessary to maintain, improve, or restore the physical, psychologic, or economic health or safety of the employee or the employee's family member or to protect those who associate or work with the employee.
  • Employees will receive the required Notices/Posting of Rights under the New York City and New York State Paid Sick Leave Laws.

Paid Sick Leave will be paid at the Employees' regular rate of pay in effect. If the employee does not have a regular rate of pay, the annual average rate of pay will be used.

All earned and unused Paid Sick Leave will be deposited into the employees' 401(a) account upon termination of employment (at the current rate). For purposes of this policy, termination will occur when the employee is affirmatively discharged by the Company, resigns voluntarily, or after 6 months of inactive status in the Company.

Except where stated otherwise in this policy, all employees can use all Paid Sick Leave accrued under this policy as soon as the Paid Sick Leave is accrued – there is no waiting period for using Paid Sick Leave. Except as otherwise required by law, Employees are eligible to use all accumulated hours of available accrued or carried over Paid Sick Leave per year.

Paid Sick Leave must be taken in a minimum initial daily increment of four hours; however, any Paid Sick Leave beyond the initial minimum four (4) hour increment in a given day may be used in 30-minute intervals that start on the hour or half-hour.

Time taken off as Paid Sick Leave will not be considered hours worked for purposes of overtime pay.

It is the Employees' responsibility to notify the Company of all absences as soon as possible. Where the use of Paid Sick Leave is foreseeable, Employees are expected to provide seven days' advance notice of the intention to use Paid Sick Leave. An Employee who uses Paid Sick Leave for an unforeseeable reason must provide notice as soon as practicable.

The Company will not unlawfully retaliate against Employees for requesting or using Paid Sick Leave for for filing a complaint for alleged violations of the law, for communicating with any person, including coworkers, about any violation of the law, for participating in a court proceeding regarding an alleged violation of the law or for informing another person of that person's potential rights under the law.

The Company will not require the disclosure of details relating to an employee's or his or her family member's medical condition or require the disclosure of details relating to an employee's or his or her family member's status as a victim of family offenses, sexual offenses, stalking, or human trafficking as a condition of providing Paid Sick Leave. Health information about an employee or an employee's family member, and information concerning an employee's or his or her family member's status or perceived status as a victim of family offenses, sexual offenses, stalking or human trafficking obtained solely for the purposes of utilizing leave under this policy will be treated as confidential and will not be disclosed except by the affected employee, with the written permission of the affected employee or as required by law.

Employees on leave pursuant to applicable federal, state, and/or local law may be required to use any accrued Paid Sick Leave for such absences. However, Employees will not be required to use available Paid Sick Leave during a period of New York Paid Family Leave. Paid Sick Leave will not accrue during any leave of absence or time off from work.

Acknowledgment of Receipt of the Company's Paid Sick Leave Policy and Notice of Employee Rights:

By my signature below, I acknowledge that I have received copies of the X-treme Care LLC's Paid Sick Leave Policy (2022 Revision) and a Notices of Employee Rights and that I have been given opportunity to read and consider such documents.

For Existing Employees Only:

I further knowlege that during the course of my employment with the Company, I am aware that the Company maintained a Paid Sick Leave policy and practices of allowing its Employees, including me, to take Paid Sick Leave. I have always been given full opportunity to take time off.

sub_forms.content:
FAIR AND IMPARTIAL RESOLUTION ("FAIR") ARBITRATION AGREEMENT FOR PERSONAL ASSISTANTS

Doc. No: XTC-LGL10_rev.01

This Fair and Impartial Resolution Arbitration Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered into between X-treme Care, LLC (the "Agency") and the undersigned Personal Assistant (the "Personal Assistant").

Condition of Commencement of Work

As a condition of commencement or continuation of work, the Personal Assistant agrees that any and all claims, disputes, or controversies of any kind, arising out of or relating to employment with the Agency or the termination of employment with the Agency (including, but not limited to, claims arising under federal, state and local statutory law, common law, and employment contracts) shall be subject to binding arbitration as provided in this Agreement.

Mutual Agreement to Arbitrate

The Personal Assistant and Agency mutually agree that any Covered Claims will be decided by binding arbitration administered by ADR Systems or the American Arbitration Association (AAA) under their Employment Arbitration Rules & Mediation Procedures. Covered Claims include, without limitation, claims arising under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), the New York Human Rights Law, the New York Labor Law, and all other federal, state, and local statutory, common law, contract, tort, and equitable claims.

Excluded Claims and Charges

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following claims and charges are excluded from the scope of this arbitration agreement and may be brought in court: (a) workers' compensation claims; (b) unemployment insurance claims; (c) claims that by law cannot be subject to mandatory arbitration; and (d) claims or charges filed with administrative agencies (such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, or state fair employment agencies) that are not subject to a private right of action under law; provided, however, that any right to monetary relief with respect to such agency claims must be pursued in arbitration if it is subject to a private right of action.

Arbitration Procedure

Any Covered Claim will be decided by a single neutral third-party arbitrator outside of court and without a jury. The arbitrator, and not any court or agency, shall have exclusive authority to resolve any dispute relating to the interpretation, applicability, enforceability of this Agreement, including but not limited to any dispute regarding the arbitrability of any dispute, except for a dispute regarding the limitation that any Covered Claim must be heard in arbitration on an individual, bilateral basis only, which shall be determined only by a court of competent jurisdiction.

To initiate arbitration of a Covered Claim, a Party must file a written demand in accordance with the ADR Systems Rules for starting the arbitration process. Arbitration of a Covered Claim must be commenced within the same time limitations prescribed by the statute of limitations applicable to the Covered Claim being asserted. Any arbitration under this Agreement will take place in the county and state in which Personal Assistant most recently worked for the Agency, or, if that venue is not convenient for the parties, another location that is reasonably convenient for the parties and selected by the arbitrator.

Each Party shall pay its own filing fees to commence the arbitration. The filing fee is nonrefundable per ADR rules. Above and beyond the filing fees, and irrespective of the ADR System rules, all other fees and costs associated with administration of any arbitration under ADR will be split equally between the parties, with each party paying an equal share of such fees and costs. Employee and Agency will each bear their own attorneys' fees, except as otherwise provided by law.

The arbitrator must apply the substantive law, including the applicable burdens of proof and persuasion that would be applied by a court of competent jurisdiction hearing the Covered Claim. The arbitrator may grant any appropriate relief that could be granted by a court hearing the Covered Claim, but will not have any authority to grant any other relief. The arbitrator shall not have the authority to consolidate more than one person's claims or to preside over any form of a class, collective, representative, or joint proceeding. Personal Assistant and Agency waive the right to in any way bring or participate in any class, collective, representative, or joint action or proceeding concerning any Covered Claim that is heard in court and waive the right to a jury trial for any such Covered Claim.

This Agreement and Personal Assistant's employment with Agency affect interstate commerce and, therefore, any arbitration shall be governed solely by the Federal Arbitration Act (9 U.S.C. Secs. 1-16) and not any state law concerning arbitration.

Confidentiality

Any arbitration proceeding initiated under this provision, together with all materials related to such arbitration (such as pleadings, briefs, transcripts, motions, decisions, evidence etc.) shall be confidential and private in all respects, and to the maximum extent permitted by law, not disclosed or disseminated to others.

Survival and Severability

This Agreement terms shall survive the termination of Personal Assistant's employment with Agency, regardless of the reason for or circumstances surrounding such termination.

If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid or unenforceable, its remaining provisions shall remain valid and enforceable, and the provision found to be invalid or unenforceable shall be reformed, to the extent possible, to make it valid and enforceable in accordance with the Parties' intent herein and applicable law, except that if the limitation of any Covered Claim heard in arbitration on an individual, bilateral basis only is found to be void, unenforceable, or substantially limited, then this Agreement shall be null and void with regard to such Covered Claim, subject to any right to appeal such determination, but this Agreement shall remain valid and enforceable with respect to all other Covered Claims.

Protected Rights

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, nothing in this Agreement is intended to or will be construed to limit Personal Assistant's rights, to the extent protected under law, to file a charge or complaint or otherwise communicate with a governmental agency changed with the enforcement of any law.

Amendment

Agency reserves the right to amend or terminate this Agreement. Such amendments may be made by providing notice to Personal Assistant, electronically or otherwise, of such amendment or termination. Any amendments will be prospective only. Personal Assistant's continuation of employment after receiving notice of any amendment or to or termination of this Agreement will be deemed agreement to such amendment or termination.

BY EXECUTING THIS AGREEMENT, PERSONAL ASSISTANT AND AGENCY UNDERSTAND AND AGREE THAT THEY ARE GIVING UP THE RIGHT TO A JURY TRIAL, THE RIGHT TO FILE A LAWSUIT IN COURT AGAINST THE OTHER, AND THE RIGHT TO BRING OR PARTICIPATE IN A CLASS OR COLLECTIVE ACTION AGAINST THE OTHER IN COURT OR IN ARBITRATION REGARDING ANY COVERED CLAIMS.

FURTHER, BY SIGNING THIS AGREEMENT, PERSONAL ASSISTANT UNDERSTANDS AND AGREES THAT PERSONAL ASSISTANT HAS HAD BEEN GIVEN THE OPPORTUNITY TO FULLY REVIEW THIS ENTIRE AGREEMENT, UNDERSTAND THE TERMS, AND IS VOLUNTARILY ENTERING INTO TO IT. PERSONAL ASSISTANT'S EXECUTION OF THIS AGREEMENT DOES NOT MODIFY THE AT-WILL NATURE OF PERSONAL ASSISTANT'S EMPLOYMENT WITH AGENCY.

In witness whereof, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the date(s) indicated below, and by such execution, agree to be bound by the terms of this Agreement.

HOME HEALTH AIDE AGREEMENT TO MAINTAIN CONFIDENTIALITY AND NOT TO SOLICIT CLIENTS, PATIENTS, OR EMPLOYEES

Doc. No: XTC-LGL11_rev.00

This binding Agreement is made on (date) {{non_solicitation__agreement_date}}, between X-treme Care, LLC., the , a Employer ("X-treme" or "Employer"), and the Employee, (name) {{non_solicitation__employee_print_name}} HHA/PCA employed by X-treme ("Employee" or "HHA").

1. Employment of HHA/PCA by X-treme

X-treme has agreed to hire or to continue to employ the Employee as an HHA/PCA, and to assign the Employee to perform home health care and other home assistance services for one or more Clients or Patients of X-treme ("Clients/Patients"). In exchange for Employee signing and entering into this Agreement, X-treme will hire, or will continue to employ, the Employee to perform such services on an employment-at-will basis, going forward, with the understanding that there is no specified period of time or duration of promised employment.

2. Clients/Patients Introduced by X-treme

  • a. By employing Employee as set forth above, X-treme agrees to provide one or more Clients/Patients for whom Employee will perform home health care or similar home assistance services, and to introduce those Clients/Patients of X-treme to Employee.
  • b. Employee acknowledges that each such Client/Patient of X-treme has been introduced to the Employee by X-treme, and that, if Employee had not been hired and assigned cases by X-treme, Employee would not have been introduced to any of X-treme's Clients/Patients, and Employee would not have had an opportunity to perform home health care or similar home assistance services for those Clients/Patients of X-treme.
  • c. Employee further acknowledges that introductions to X-treme's Clients/Patients is a valuable privilege, and that X-treme maintains a continuing interest in its business relationship and health care relationship with each of its Clients/Patients for whom Employee is assigned to perform services.

3. Employee's Covenant Not To Solicit or Take Away X-treme's Clients/Patients

  • a. The Employee acknowledges that he or she has been provided access and introductions to, and hasbean given the opportunity to form working relationships with Clients/Patients of X-treme, that would not have been available to the Employee had he or she not been hired and given continued employment by X-treme. Accordingly, Employee agrees that Employee will not use these introductions and working relationships with Clients/Patients of X-treme to harm X-treme, or to the detriment or disadvantage of X-treme's business.
  • b. Employee hereby agrees, for the entire time he or she is employed by X-treme, and for a period of one (1) year after Employee's employment with X-treme ends for any reason:
    • (i) Employee shall not remove or attempt to remove, divert or take away the business and Client-relationship existing between X-treme and any of its Clients/Patients, for the benefit of any other agency or any other entity or employer performing similar services, or for the benefit of the Employee seeking to perform such home care services on his or her own; and
    • (ii) Employee shall not solicit or request of any Client/Patient of X-treme to leave X-treme, orcause or attempt to cause such Client/Patient to leave or end its business or Client-relationship with X-treme, for the benefit of any other agency, entity or employer, or for the benefit of the Employee seeking to perform such home care services on his or her own; and
    • (iii) Employee shall not conspire or collaborate with any other employees of X-treme, or witany other or alternative agency, entity or employer performing such services, to solicit, remove or attempt to remove, divert, or take away any Client/Patient of X-treme, through any direct or indirect means; and
    • (iv) Employee shall not perform services for any Client/Patient of X-treme as an employee of any other agency, entity or employer performing home care related services, or by Employee working on his/her own, if such Client/Patient of X-treme was solicited, removed, diverted or taken away from X-treme in violation of this Agreement.
  • c. For the purposes of this Agreement, a Client/Patient shall mean and be understood to include any Client/Patient of X-treme who has received services from X-treme or its personnel within three (3) months prior to the date of the first attempt by Employee to solicit, divert, or take away the Client/Patient from its business relationship with X-treme; and excludes any Client/Patient who was brought to X-treme exclusively by the efforts of the Employee and with whom X-treme had no prior relationship.

4. Employee's Covenant Not to Solicit or Take Away Other X-treme Employees

Employee acknowledges that, as a result of being hired by and employed by X-treme, Employee was introduced to other X-treme personnel working in the Employee's field. Accordingly, during the entire period of Employee s employment by X-treme, and for a period of one (1) year after Employee's employment with X-treme ends for any reason:

  • (i) Employee shall not solicit or request any other employee of X-treme to leave employment with X-treme, or cause or attempt to cause such person to end an existing employment relationship with X-treme and to instead work for another employer, agency, or entity, or to work on their own; and
  • (ii) Employee shall not conspire or collaborate any agency, entity or other employer to solicit, divert, or take away any employees of X-treme, whether through direct or indirect means.

5. Employee's Covenant Not to Disclose Patient's Confidential Information

  • a. Employee acknowledges that, in the course of his or her duties while employed by X-treme, Employee has been or may become privileged to see and learn certain private, personal, and Confidential Information concerning Clients/Patients of X-treme, including but not limited to: Client/Patient medical and protected health information and patient identifying information, which may be subject to legal protection from disclosure. Employer further acknowledges that X-treme has a business interest in maintaining the privacy of all such Confidential Information.
  • b. Employee acknowledges that Employee has received training as to what constitutes protected health information and patient identifying information under HIPAA (the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act), and has been trained as to his or her obligations to preserve the privacy of this Confidential Information.
  • c. In order to protect the privacy such Confidential Information for the benefit of the Client/Patient, X-treme, and the Employee, Employee hereby agrees to preserve and protect the privacy of personal information of the Patient/Client, and all medical and protected health information of the Patient/Client, including but not limited to patient identifying information (such as: last names, addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, medical conditions, diagnoses, symptoms, medical records, and any other personal or protected health information, Social Security Numbers, bank account numbers, and other personal or private information of the Client/Patient) (together, "Confidential Information"), and not to disclose or reveal any such Confidential Information to any outside or third parties (other than to X-treme supervisory personnel authorized to receive such information, or as may be required in the course of Employee's direct care of the Client/Patient).

6. Employer's Remedies for Breach of this Agreement.

  • a. Employee acknowledges that a breach, or threatened breach of this Agreement by Employee would cause or threaten irreparable harm to X-treme which cannot be reasonably calculated or adequately compensated in money dam ages. Accordingly, Employee acknowledges that, in the event of any breach or threatened breach by Employee, X-treme shall be entitled to, and Employee hereby consents to, the issuance of equitable and injunctive relief to restrain and enjoin any such breach or threatened breach by Employee, which remedy shall be issued by any court of competent jurisdiction without the posting of a bond (which is hereby waived), together with reimbursement of X-treme's reasonable costs and attorneys' fees expended in obtaining such relief, in addition to any other remedies which may be available to the X-treme. Such remedies shall inure to the benefit of X-treme or its parent company, subsidiaries and affiliates, and their respective successors and assigns.
  • b. It is expressly agreed by Employee that the nature and scope of each of the provisions set forth in Paragraphs 1 through 6 of this Agreement are reasonable and necessary for the protection of the X-treme 's legitimate business interests. If, for any reason, any provision or any aspect of any provision as applied to Employee, is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to be unreasonable, overbroad or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified only to such extent as is required to make the provision reasonable and/or enforceable, as the case may be.

By Employee's signature below, Employee acknowledges that he or she has read and fully understands this Agreement, and knows that it prohibits Employee from taking away, or attempting to take away, X- treme's Clients/Patients, or X-treme's other employees, and prohibits Employee from disclosing any Client's or Patient's Confidential Information and patient identifying information.

sub_forms.content:
One-Employee Shift Acknowledgement

Doc. No: XTC-LGL15_rev.00

We encourage our employees to take their required duty-free, uninterrupted meal breaks. As you know, however, the nature of the home care industry in which we operate can, necessitate that only one personal care aide or home health aide may be on duty at any given time while working in the patient's home. In those situations, home care aides and/or personal care aides must therefore maintain supervision over the disabled individuals under their care and be ready to assist them whenever necessary. Given the circumstances and responsibilities of this industry and the home care aide/personal care aide job requirements and working conditions, we anticipate that you will not always be able to take an uninterrupted, duty-free meal break. This is because there may be times when no other aide would be available to supervise the patient while you are on your meal break.

We are therefore requesting that you consider consenting to an arrangement where you would agree to eat your meals on the job without being relieved of your duties during those times when no other aide would be present to supervise the patient. If you agree to this arrangement, you will still receive meal breaks, but you would likely need to work through all or part of your meal periods during the times in question. You will be paid for any meal periods that you work through, in whole or in part. If you choose not to sign this consent, we will work to ensure that you receive your uninterrupted, duty-free meal periods.

If you agree to the arrangement detailed above, please sign and date in the appropriate spaces below. By signing below, you acknowledge that your decision to accept this arrangement was made knowingly, voluntarily, and of your own free will, free from any duress or coercion. If you have any questions, please let us know.

Sincerely,

I voluntarily consent to the one-employee shift arrangement described above. I understand that the nature of the home care industry may necessitate one-employee shifts and that my meal periods may be interrupted by calls to duty. sub_forms.title: Travel Time Pay Policy
sub_forms.content:
Travel Time Pay Acknowledgement

Doc. No: XTC-LGL18_rev.00

I, {{travel_time_pay__print_name}}, certify my agreement and understanding of the language below regarding the calculation of pay for travel time.

To ensure caregivers are paid properly for travel time, X-treme Care, LLC. (XTC) will pay for travel time in 15-minute increments. XTC will pay travel time based on GPS information either by walking or public transportation times from one location to the second within the 5 boroughs of NYC. For travel time occurring outside of the 5 boroughs of NYC, it will be computed based on GPS times for either walking or driving. If the computed travel time based on GPS for walking exceeds 15 min by walking, XTC will automatically pay based on public transportation times or driving based on the location as mentioned previously.

If your actual travel time exceeds the assumption of how much time you spent commuting between shifts, or you notice an error in your pay for work travel, you must let your coordinator know in order to receive the correct payment of travel time.

Compliance Program Acknowledgement

Compliance Program

Dear Staff Member:

X-treme Care is dedicated to conducting its business honestly and ethically, wherever X-treme Care operates. In order to meet this commitment, X-treme Care has set forth in this Code of Conduct the principles and rules to be followed by all personnel who work with X-treme Care. The purpose of this Code of Conduct is to inform all personnel and interested third parties that X-treme Care is fully dedicated to approaching all of its activities, including compliance with laws and regulations, in an ethical manner. This Code of Conduct will familiarize new personnel with the ethical standards that guide our business and patient relationships in our highly regulated environment. For existing personnel, it will reaffirm our commitment to ethical behavior in all circumstances. Since everyone at X-treme Care has a personal stake in this important program, we strongly urge each of you to review this information thoroughly and refer to it whenever situations arise requiring you to exercise your judgment.

Compliance with laws, regulations and our policies require the full commitment of all X-treme Care personnel. Each of us is personally and professionally responsible for understanding and adhering to this Code of Conduct and the supporting policies and procedures, including those areas covering your specific job responsibilities. The purpose of this Code of Conduct is to provide you with guidance on ethical and compliance issues. However, this Code of Conduct cannot cover every issue you may encounter. If you have a question or encounter a situation which concerns you, you should ask for X-treme Care through your department supervisor, the Administrator and/or the Compliance Officer.

I, {{driving_policy__print_name}},certify that I have been trained on the X-treme Care Driving Policy. I understand driving a patient's vehicle or being a passenger in a patient's vehicle is strictly forbidden and is not allowed under any circumstance. Transporting a patient in their vehicle or any vehicle is also strictly forbidden and is not allowed under any circumstance. Public or private for hire transportation must be utilized to transport patients.

Any violation of this policy is grounds for immediate termination. This policy is meant for the patient's protection, your protection and the company's protection.
